body:
The original routing acceptance is supported by the existing evidence, as detailed in the [acceptance audit](https://github.com/wrbell/stark-translate/blob/main/docs/evaluation/mac_followup_20260910/tts-routing-acceptance.md).

- Actual operator controls selected local TTS with independent English **MacBook Pro Speakers** and Spanish **Microsoft Teams Audio** routes; the selections survived reload and an owned idle operator restart.
- The production Piper engine and device resolver opened the matching native devices, completed host playback, and closed without callback errors or fallback in both the stock-voice run and the explicit-path retest. The original failed explicit-path attempt is retained, followed by its fix and passing retest.
- Focused tests cover the real operator/CLI fields, language routing, Piper device forwarding, persistence and retry/fallback. The Python 3.11 and 3.12 test jobs [passed on `4b0144d`](https://github.com/wrbell/stark-translate/actions/runs/34502608307).

This satisfies the issue's selected-output and independent EN/ES routing scope, including its explicitly allowed virtual-output path. The language map selects the output for the spoken target language; it does not duplicate each caption to two outputs.

The operator and native checks were separate: full caption-triggered native playback, virtual far-end reception, human-heard output and physical unplug/replug remain separate service-validation gates. The nearby microphone sessions had TTS off. No new device tests were run for this audit, and closure does not certify those pending gates or change model defaults.
